_comment_1: Rule 6(1)(e) LMPC 2011 - a retail sale price the label declares EXCLUSIVE of all taxes. LM-PC-0005 asks whether a price was declared at all; this asks one narrow question about how it was declared.
_comment_2: STEP 3. LM-PC-0005's own _comment_4 recorded the gap and its size: 'PRESENCE ONLY, AND THIS ONE UNDER-CLAIMS THE MOST. Clause (e) requires the price to be clearly indicated as the maximum retail price inclusive of all taxes in Indian currency. That is a FORMAT requirement and no format check is registered.' This rule closes a SLICE of that gap and leaves the rest open, deliberately.
_comment_3: WHAT IS CHECKED: exactly one thing - that the label does not declare the price EXCLUSIVE of all taxes. labelextract reads the printed words next to the price and records inclusive_of_all_taxes: false when it sees them. Nothing about that reading is interpretive, and a price declared exclusive of all taxes contradicts both clause (e) and the rule 2(m) definition.
_comment_4: WHAT IS NOT CHECKED, AND WHY EACH IS LEFT ALONE. (1) The ABSENCE of an 'inclusive of all taxes' indication is NOT a violation here: whether printing 'MRP' alone already clearly indicates tax inclusion - rule 2(m) defines the term as inclusive - is a question of legal construction, and this project does not invent legal tests. It is recorded in the finding's diagnostics as observed or not observed. (2) 'In Indian currency' is NOT checked at all: normalise_price writes currency 'INR' as a fixed DEFAULT, not as a reading, so testing the clause against it would be testing our own default and reporting it as evidence about the package. (3) Whether the price is the true maximum is not knowable from a package - that is rule 18(2), about the price actually charged.
_comment_5: Applicability and category targeting are IDENTICAL to LM-PC-0005's: proviso (C) for bidi and for domestic LPG cylinders priced under the Administrative Price Mechanism, and alcoholic beverages where State Excise Laws provide for the declaration, are carried as conditions on the clause's RuleRequirement and resolved before this validator runs. requires_applicability_conditions is true.
title: Retail sale price must not be declared exclusive of taxes
requirement: Where a retail sale price is declared, the package must not declare it exclusive of all taxes. Only that is checked. Whether the price is clearly indicated as the maximum retail price, whether it is in Indian currency, and whether it is the true maximum are NOT checked by this rule.
legal_reference: Rule 6(1)(e) of the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
source_note: Checked 2026-08-30 by Claude Code (automated legal-source check) for raghavrrrao against the Department of Consumer Affairs (Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution) consolidated publication 'Book on Legal Metrology Packaged Commodities Rules, 2011 with all amendments', https://consumeraffairs.gov.in/public/upload/admin/cmsfiles/whatsnews/Book_on_Legal_Metrology_Packaged_Commodities_Rules,2011_with_all_amendments_whatsnews.pdf (sha256 0ef948f9c6b89f5dfb20d384861901714fd0dc54fc67b5b86c772d2c3f983a4b; server Last-Modified 2025-04-14). Clause (e) reads there, verbatim: 'the retail sale price of the package;', followed by the words substituted vide G.S.R. 629(E) dated 23rd June 2017 w.e.f. 1.1.2018: 'shall clearly indicate that it is the maximum retail price inclusive of all taxes in Indian currency:'. The source records that the illustrations and rounding words which followed were replaced by the words 'in Indian currency' vide G.S.R. 779(E) dated 2nd November 2021 w.e.f. 1.4.2022, now w.e.f. 01.10.2022 vide G.S.R. 226(E) dated 28th March 2022 - which is the wording in force and the wording this rule is written against, NOT the pre-2018 or pre-2022 text. Rule 2(m), as substituted vide G.S.R. 629(E), defines 'retail sale price' verbatim as 'the maximum price at which the commodity in packaged form may be sold to the consumer inclusive of all taxes'. Proviso (C) to rule 6(1) reads verbatim: 'no declaration as to the retail sale price shall be required to be made on (i) any package containing bidi; (ii) any domestic liquefied petroleum gas cylinder of which the price is covered under the Administrative Price Mechanism of the Government.'
